lawyer:
Ziaur Rahman Khan, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners 
Shaukat Ali Khan, Md Tamizuddin, Fazlul Haque Khan Fakir, Rahen Hossain with Moztafa Zaman Islam; Advocates ----- For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Tofazzal Hossain (Md) and others ------ Petitioners
vs
Momtaz Begum & others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
In this Rule, the judgment and order dated 15-4-99 passed by the Second Court of Subordinate Judge, Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 2 of 1997 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and order dated 30-1-97 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Saturia in the District of Manikganj in Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 5 of 1995, allowing the pre-emption have been called in question.

2. Broad facts leading to the case are that, opposite party No. 1 as per-emptor instituted a case in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Saturia being Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No. 5 of 1995 for pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. The case of the pre-emptor, in short, is that Koran All was the owner of the case jote by way of inheritance and purchase. He died leaving son Bachchu Mia, three daughters namely Momtaz Begum, Samiran and Hazera Khatun in opposite party Nos. 3 and 4. While Bachchu Mia was owning and possessing the case land in ejmali with his sisters, he gifted the case land to his wife Hazera Begum by a heba-bil-ewaz deed dated 20-12-89. Hazera Begum subsequently sold the case land to the petitioners by a kabala dated 21-12-94 at a consideration of Taka 60,000.00. It is against this sale the pre-emptor filed the pre-emption case as a co-sharer by inheritance to the case jote.

3. The petitioners as opposite parties contested the case by filling written objection denying the material allegations of the pre-emption application contending; inter alia, that after purchase they duly mutated their names in respect of the case land and the jama has been duly separated following which they have been paying rent to the Government Acquired Estate and, consequently, the pre-emptor is no longer a co-sharer to the case jote and she is not competent to maintain the pre-emption case.

4. At the trial, the pre-emptor examined 3 witnesses and contesting opposite parties examined 4 witnesses and exhibited documents in support of their respective cases.

5. The learned Assistant Judge by his impugned judgment and order dated 30-1-97 allowed pre-emption with the finding that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer by inheritance to the case jote and the parent jama has not been separated in accordance with law as a result or which the parent jama remains intact. The learned Assistant Judge further found that on fraudulent suppression of material facts and all legal processes the pre-emptees obtained an order of mutation in their favour and as such, this fraudulent exercise does not in any way affect the pre-emptor's right of pre-emption.

6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order the pre-emptees took an appeal before the District Judge, Manikganj, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 2 of 1997, and the learned Second Court of Subordinate Judge who heard the appeal, has been' pleased by the impugned judgment and order dated 15-4-99 to dismiss the appeal affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court. It is against this judgment the pre-emptees moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr Ziaur Rahman Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Courts below erred in law in allowing pre-emption holding without any lawful basis, that the jama in question was not legally separated and the same has occasioned failure of justice. The learned Counsel further submits that the learned Courts below erred in law in not properly discussing and considering the material evidence on record and the same has also occasioned failure of justice.

8. Mr Shawkat Ali Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 on the other hand, submits that the learned Courts below on detailed discussion and consideration of the material evidence on record concurrently found that the Jama in question was not separated according to law as a result of which the parent jama remained intact and the pre-emptor continues to be a co-sharer to the case/jote. The pre-emptor has also been found entitled to pre-emption on all other counts under the law. These concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the learned Court below, argues Mr Khan, being well reasoned and well-supported by the evidence on record are immune from attack in revision under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.

9. The learned Counsel appearing for the petitioners has placed before me the impugned Judgments of the learned Courts below. In this case it is an undisputed fact that the case land belonged to Koran Ali Sk. It is also not disputed that the pre-emptor Momtaz Begum is one of the daughters of Koran Ali Sk. It is not also disputed that Bachchu Miah is the son of Koran Ali Sk. who has gifted the suit land to his wife Hajera Begum, the vendor of the disputed kabala. Evidently, pre-emptor opposite party No. 1 is a co-sharer to the case jote by inheritance.

10. The main defence of the petitioners at the moment appears to be that it has not been proved that the jama in question was not separated in accordance with the provision of section 117 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and, as such, the parent jama no longer exists, rendering the pre-emptor a non-co-sharer to the case jote. Mr Ziaur Rahman Khan argues that the case records of Mutation Case No. 68/1990-91 before the Upazila Revenue Officer, Saturia have not been legally brought on record in this case to prove that the order of mutation was passed in favour of vendor Mrs. Hajera Begum on fraudulent suppression of the legal processes and, as such, the learned Courts below erred in law in holding that the jama in question has not been separated in accordance with la as a result of which the finding on separation of the jama is without any legal basis.

11. It appears that this case has a chequered career. After the pre-emption case was allowed by the learned Assistant Judge, the pre-emptees took an appeal before the District Judge, Manikganj being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 2 of 1997, but the said appeal was eventually dismissed on contest by the judgment and order dated 30-1-97. Against the aforesaid judgment and order the petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 1272 of 1998. This Court by the judgment dated 18-11-98 made the Rule absolute and sent back the appeal on remand to the learned Subordinate Judge, Manikganj for a fresh hearing in accordance with law and in the light of the observations made in the body of the judgment. The only ground of objection in the aforesaid revision urged by the petitioners at the hearing of the revision case was that the relevant SA Khatian containing the name of the pre-emptor, along with others, was not legally brought on record and the petitioners are, therefore entitled to an opportunity to verify the genuineness of the said SA Khatian proving co-sharer ship of the pre-emptor in the jote. The question of separation of the case jama was never raised at that time and no objection was taken thereon.

12. After the appeal went back on remand for a fresh hearing, the learned Court of appeal below allowed additional evidence to the parties and after hearing the contending parties, dismissed the appeal affirming the judgment and order passed by the learned trial Court. It appears that while disposing of the appeal on remand, the learned Subordinate Judge duly considered all material aspects of the case and the material evidence on record and concurred with the material findings arrived at by the learned trial Court. It is found that the question of not legally bringing on record the case records of Mutation Case No. 68/1990-91 was never raised before the learned appellate Court. Mr Ziaur Rahman Khan argues that since the records of the aforesaid Mutation Case were not legally brought on record proving separation of the Jama, the case should be sent back on remand once again to the learned Court of appeal below to prove the fact of separation of the Jama.

13. It has been concurrently found by the learned Courts below with reference to the evidence on record that the jama in question has not been separated in accordance with law and the pre-emptor continues to be a co-sharer to the case jote. It has also been found that the so-called order of mutation was obtained fraudulently and collusively a result of which the right of pre-emption for the pre-emptor remains unaffected. It appears from order No. 39 dated 13-11-96 passed by the learned Assistant Judge. Saturia that he called for the records of Mutation Case No. 68 of 1990-91 filed by vendor Hajera Begum from the office of the Upazila Revenue Officer, Saturia and the aforesaid case records were produced before the learned trial Court by a special messenger and since then the said records are lying with the case records of the present pre-emption case. The parties thus had full view and complete knowledge of the case records of Mutation Case No. 68 of 1990-91 and they led evidence in the case with reference to the facts of the said mutation proceedings. It is found from the evidence of the pre-emptor appearing as PW 1 that she clearly stated in her evidence that the disputed mutation proceeding was filed against three dead persons named Koran Sk. Khatemon Bibi and Ameton Bibi and the petitioner of the said mutation case fraudulently obtained the so-called order of mutation in her favour on fraudulent suppression of facts without bringing on record the legal representatives of the said dead persons. She also stated in her evidence that neither she nor any of the heirs and heiresses of Koran Sk. was made a party to the said mutation case. She also stated that her fufus Khateman Bibi and Ameton Bibi were also dead at the time of filing of the mutation case and they left behind heirs and heiresses to succeed them.

14. DW 1 Tofazzal Hossain stated in his examination-in-chief that Koran Ali died leaving two sons and three daughters and thereafter Khateman died leaving Jalil and Wahab as her two sons while Ametan died leaving sons Habibur, Mozibor and Mashuk. It is evident from the mutation case records that the heirs and heiresses of the aforesaid dead persons named Koran Sk Khateman and Ametan Bibi were not substituted in the mutation case in question. It is also evident from the report of the process-server that Koran Sk was dead at the relevant time and notice could not be served on him. The death of the recorded tenant Koran Sk before the filing of the mutation case is an established fact in this case and the fact that his legal heirs and heiresses including the pre-emptor, were not substituted in the mutation proceeding, is also an undisputed fact. In the facts of the case and the evidence on record, it is manifestly evident that the so-called order of mutation in favour of vendor Hazera Begum is fraudulent, collusive and void and, as such, it is of no legal consequence as a result of which and consequently the parent Khatian remains intact and the pre-emptor continues to be a co-sharer to the case jote by inheritance. The concurrent findings of fact on this score arrived at by the learned Courts below are well-founded by the evidence on record and the law bearing on the subject. In view of the fact that the parent jama has not been separated in accordance with law with proper notice upon all the co-sharers, the so-called order of mutation cannot defeat the right of pre-emption of the pre-emptor, who is admittedly a daughter of the original tenant Koran Sk, It is true, the records of the mutation case have not been brought on record and marked exhibits in conformity with the strict requirements of law but the admitted fact is that, the records of the mutation case are lying with the case records of the present pre-emption case since before the conclusion of the trial within the full knowledge of the parties and they led evidence at the trial with reference to the aforesaid case records of the mutation proceedings in question. So, it cannot at all be said that the pre-emptees were in any way prejudiced due to the technical fault of not marking the records of the mutation case as exhibit in the present case. Since the contending parties took full advantage of the' case records of the mutation proceedings in question and since the pre-emptees did not raise any objection on this technicality at any point of time earlier, there can be no logic for sending back the case on remand once again for meeting the untenable technical objection, which caused no prejudice to the petitioner. I think, this new question of fact raised before this Court for the first time now deserves no serious consideration. I am of the view that the learned Courts below committed no error of law in taking notice of Mutation Case No. 68/1990-91 in reaching their conclusions on the basis of other consistent and reliable evidence on record.

<u>15. Mr Shaukat Ali Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the opposite party has cited before me the case of Md Karimullah Bhuiyan vs Hazi Nurul Alam Chowdhury, reported in 35 DLR (AD) 338. In this case it has been held that court of law is fully competent in a pre-emption proceeding to see whether the splitting up of the jama was made in accordance with the provisions of section 117(1)(c) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. In our case under review, the learned Courts below duly noticed and considered the patent illegality and fraud committed in obtaining the so-called order of mutation in favour of vendor Hazera Bibi. On the face of the record, it is manifestly evident that vendor Hazera Bibi obtained the order of mutation in their favour in Mutation Case No. 68/1990-91 by fraudulent suppression of all legal processes and that too against three dead persons without substituting their legal representatives. It was evidently a collusive and fraudulent exercise with oblique motives and that in no anyway separated the parent jama as a result of which the original jama remains intact and the pre-emptor continues to be a co-sharer by inheritance. These findings of fact arrived at by the learned Courts below are well-reasoned and well-supported by the materials on record and these do not suffer from any illegality or any legal infirmity occasioning failure of justice so as to justify interference by this Court exercising revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure.</u>

16. Mr Ziaur Rahman Khan, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submits that, in the interest of justice the case should be sent back on remand for clarifying the question of separation of the jama, which is the real bone of contention between the contending parties.

17. In view of the fact that the question of separation of the jama has been elaborately discussed and considered by the learned Courts below in the light of the evidence on record and the pre-emptee petitioners took no objection at any point of time on the question of not formally bringing the records of the Mutation Case and they played their full cycles at the trial, I do not find it necessary for making a second order of remand prolonging an already old and unworthy legal battle. In view of the concurrent findings of fact arrived at by the learned Courts below that the pre-emptor is a co-sharer to the case jote and the parent jama has not been separated in accordance with law and these findings of fact being well supported by the evidence on record, the prayer for remand deserves no consideration as it would serve no useful purpose. The learned Courts below duly addressed themselves to this moot question and rightly decided it on the basis of evidence. I do not, therefore, find any substance in the submissions made by the learned Court for the pre-emptees. The impugned judgments are well-reasoned and well-supported by the materials on record and these do not suffer from any illegality or legal infirmity justifying interference by this Court exercising revisional power under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure. I do not find any merit in the revision case.

18. It deserves to be noted in this connection that the case records of Mutation Case No. 68 of 1990-91 clearly reveal that the application for mutation was not made by vendor Mst. Hajera Begum but it was filed in her name by one Md. Suruz Miah, who is in no way connected with the case land. It is unfortunate that the Upazila Revenue Officer in hot haste pressed the so-called order of mutation in favour of Hazera Begum in a most casual manner even without caring to see who was the applicant in the case and that all the three opposite parties in the case were dead persons. This also smacks of blatant malafides and patent collusion in the order of mutation dated 13-3-91 made in Mutation Case No. 68 of 1990-91.

19. In the result, the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs and the impugned judgment and order dated 15-4-99 passed by the learned Second Court of Subordinate Judge Manikganj in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 2 of 1997 affirming the judgment and order dated 30-11-97 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Saturia in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) No. 5 of 1995 allowing pre-emption are affirmed.

Send down the lower Court records immediately.

End.
